subject: Workplace Skills
title: Leading by Example
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Leading by Example.

hook.text: A CEO demanded work-life balance from employees but sent midnight emails. Nobody believed the policy.

buildup.text: People watch what leaders do, not what they say. Actions that contradict words destroy credibility instantly.

discovery.text: Leading by example means your behavior sets the standard. If you want punctuality, arrive first. If you want candor.

twist.text: Admitting your own mistakes publicly does more for team culture than any policy document ever could.

climax.text: Audit your actions against your stated values. Where they diverge, your team already noticed. Fix the gap.

punchline.text: Do what you say. Your team copies behavior, not words.

quiz.question: Why does leading by example matter more than verbal instructions?
options: People watch what leaders do and copy behavior, not words
Written policies are more enforceable than verbal guidance
